findings.evidence: Commit 2c236ec says 'both remaining consumers fail on 11' (typedoc and glob 7). The third excusal, minimatch 10.2.3 under @microsoft/api-extractor 7.59.2, is justified only by the reason string 'typedoc-era API needed'. api-extractor's only use of minimatch is lib-commonjs/collector/Collector.js:842 `(0, minimatch_1.minimatch)(dependencyName, packageNameOrPattern)`. Requiring minimatch 11.0.3 from CommonJS here returns that function, and minimatch('@fluxion/core','@fluxion/*') is true. So a scoped override `"@microsoft/api-extractor>minimatch": 11.0.3` would probably drop this excusal (not run: it needs a lockfile change and the API-report job). Also, [[PackageOverrides]] with vulnerability.ignore = true ignores every advisory on those exact versions, not only GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249. The commit and the comment say only that 'an advisory on any other minimatch still fails the scan'.

findings.evidence: 590e0a4's useFocusKept listens to document focusin and moves any focus outside the dialog back to Close while it is open. The <dialog> is still opened with the `open` attribute (non-modal: no top layer, no inert background), so pointer input behind it still works: a click selects on the canvas, and a click puts the caret in the library search. But keyboard focus is snapped back, so the user cannot type into a field they clicked. It works, and CI is green on all three engines. The design is a hand-made modality, though, where showModal() would give native focus containment, inert content behind the dialog and Escape handling in every engine.
findings.failure_scenario: A user clicks the library search with the Credits dialog open, types, and the keys go to the dialog: Delete and arrows are swallowed, and Escape closes the dialog. This is confusing but harmless.
